correctness.rationale: Expanding z^S over selected short bonds counts each forced nonoverlapping r-set once. Removing its endpoints cannot erase any crossing, and order-preserving relabeling preserves the rest. Shifting sorted left endpoints by 0,...,r-1 gives the path coefficient binom(2n-r,r). Differentiating gives the exact factorial identity including n=0 and r=0. The r=1 identity and uniform single-chord deletion give the stochastic comparison, hence every nondecreasing f has nonpositive covariance. The short-count variance is 2(n-1)/(2n-1). Independently, generate the matching by ranking two independent uniform endpoints for each of n labeled chords. A crossing pair has probability 1/3, the conditional crossing probability given one interval of length l is 2l(1-l), and its variance is 1/45; incident pairs yield the stated crossing variance, disjoint pairs covariance zero. These moments give the covariance and correlation as claimed. The same rank model expresses C_n as a second-order U-statistic with nonzero first projection, giving the marginal Gaussian CLT (also Flajolet–Noy Theorem 3). Fixed-r deletion changes the centering by O(n) and the standard deviation ratio by o(1). Sequential forced-bond counting gives a_{n,r}<=1 and each fixed-r factor tends to one. In the mixed transform use z=exp(is): the same factorial expansion is absolutely dominated by 2^r/r!, so the joint characteristic functions converge to the product by the continuity theorem. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py without executing frozen code. Independent bounded replay: python3 /workspace/independent_checks.py checks 238 binomial moment/crossing cells for n=0..6 plus moments and threshold inequalities; it is not evidence of joint convergence by itself.
